hero.headline: House Oversight releases transcript of Bondi interview on Epstein files
hero.teaser: The transcript shows the former attorney general declined to answer multiple questions during the four-hour closed-door session.
hero.body:
The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee released a transcript Thursday from its closed-door meeting with former Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the handling of Jeffrey Epstein files. The transcript provides the first public account of Bondi's testimony on the matter.

During the roughly four-hour session, Bondi declined to answer numerous questions. She directed responsibility to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche regarding how the files were handled.

The release of the transcript came after a contentious period between Bondi and the committee. The House panel had initially scheduled Bondi for a deposition on April 14, but the Justice Department informed the committee that she would not appear. The department argued that because Bondi no longer held the position of attorney general, the subpoena no longer applied since it had been issued in her official capacity.

The committee's Democrats responded by filing a civil contempt resolution against Bondi for not appearing at the scheduled deposition. Representative Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the committee, announced the action and stated that Bondi had "illegally defied our committee, skipped her deposition, and has refused to cooperate."

However, shortly after the Democrats announced the contempt charges, the oversight committee revealed that Bondi would appear before the panel on May 29. Republicans on the committee said the contempt action was "completely unnecessary" given that Bondi was now scheduled to testify. The oversight Democrats noted the timing, writing that the appearance was announced just 45 minutes after they filed the contempt charges.

Bondi had been subpoenaed by the committee while still serving as attorney general. The committee's chair, Republican Representative James Comer, wrote in the subpoena letter that there were questions regarding the Justice Department's handling of the Epstein investigation and its compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The Justice Department faced criticism over its compliance with that law after failing to meet a December 19 deadline to release relevant files. The department instead released what it said were the full files on January 31. Survivors of Epstein's abuse raised concerns that sensitive personal information was improperly disclosed in the files, while several lawmakers criticized some of the redactions included in the documents.

According to Democrat Garcia, Bondi had "extensive personal knowledge about the Trump administration's handling of the Epstein files," making her testimony and cooperation crucial regardless of her current job title.

The Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the matter.

cards.headline: House Democrats join Republicans to defeat Lebanon war powers resolution
cards.teaser: The House of Representatives defeated a resolution Thursday that would have constrained the Trump administration's military authority in Lebanon.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives defeated a resolution Thursday that would have limited the Trump administration's military authority in Lebanon. Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the measure, but it failed after most House Democrats joined Republicans in voting against it.

The vote exposed divisions within the Democratic caucus over Middle East policy. Democratic leadership opposed the resolution, contrasting with their support for a similar Iran war powers measure that passed the previous day. The outcome leaves the Trump administration with continued flexibility to conduct military operations in Lebanon without additional congressional constraints.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Cease-Fire Between Israel and Lebanon
cards.teaser: Hezbollah rejected a cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon that was brokered by the United States, with the group's leader calling the truce a surrend.
cards.body:
Hezbollah rejected a cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon announced by the United States following fresh diplomatic talks. The Iran-backed group's leader called the truce a surrender, noting that Hezbollah was excluded from the U.S.-brokered negotiations between the Israeli and Lebanese governments.

The rejection raises questions about the agreement's enforceability. A UN peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon, underscoring the ongoing security challenges in the region.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in Texas for first time in six decades
cards.body:
A flesh-eating parasite not seen in the United States for nearly 60 years has been confirmed in a calf in south Texas, about 50 miles from the Mexico border. The detection of the New World screwworm has alarmed agriculture officials and raised concerns about potential threats to the nation's cattle industry.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced the discovery late Wednesday, marking the first confirmed case in Texas since 1966. The parasite's larvae feed on the blood of warm-blooded animals and can spread rapidly through livestock populations if not controlled.

The screwworm was eradicated from the United States in the 1970s after causing tens of millions of dollars in losses to the livestock industry. Its return comes at a particularly sensitive time, as beef prices across the country have reached record highs. Officials worry that an outbreak could worsen food shortages and further increase prices.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture and Texas officials have been warning livestock owners about the parasite's progression through Mexico for over a year. The screwworm has advanced more than 1,100 miles from southern Mexico northward despite efforts to contain it.

Female screwworm flies lay eggs in open wounds on cattle and other animals. When the larvae hatch, they consume blood and living flesh from the host animal. Without treatment, infected animals will die.

Rollins emphasized that the situation remains manageable. "There is no threat of mass infestation," she said, noting that this is the only confirmed case so far. "There is no reason to believe this incursion will result in establishment of the pest in our country."

However, Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller expressed frustration with federal efforts, stating that the USDA has missed important components of its containment strategy. He called for increased deployment of the screwworm adult suppression system, or Swass, which uses attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides to reduce adult populations before releasing sterile flies to prevent reproduction.

Miller noted that Swass was successfully used to eradicate the screwworm in Mexico and Texas previously. "USDA already owns the playbook," he said, "the only question is whether USDA will use it before this situation gets worse."

In March, the USDA announced a partnership with the Army Corps of Engineers and Mortenson Construction to build a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas. This facility aims to support ongoing containment efforts.

The parasite poses no threat to humans or food safety directly. However, the risk to wildlife in affected areas remains a concern. Previous outbreaks, including cases in Florida in 2016 and a Maryland case in 2025, were contained without spreading further.

cards.headline: Former national security adviser John Bolton to plead guilty in classified documents case
cards.teaser: John Bolton reached a deal with prosecutors to plead guilty to charges related to his handling of classified information.
cards.body:
Former national security adviser John Bolton has reached a plea agreement with federal prosecutors over charges involving the mishandling of sensitive national security information. Bolton is expected to plead guilty to retaining classified information, according to multiple sources familiar with the case.

The deal resolves a criminal investigation into Bolton's handling of classified materials. Bolton served as national security adviser in a previous administration and has been a prominent figure in foreign policy circles. The specific charges and terms of the plea agreement have not been fully disclosed.

cards.headline: Dow Surges Nearly 900 Points to Record Close as Investors Shift Away From Tech
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed nearly 900 points to finish at a record high Wednesday, marking a significant rotation in market sentiment away from technology stocks. The rally reflected investor appetite for diversification as chip stocks stumbled following disappointing earnings reports.

Broadcom's earnings miss triggered broad weakness across the semiconductor sector. Shares of Micron and ARM also declined, dragging down chip stocks generally and weighing on the Nasdaq index. This pullback came as traders reassessed valuations in the technology space following several weeks of strong artificial intelligence stock performance.

The S&P 500 managed to overcome the technology sector weakness, posting modest gains supported by strength in other industries. The divergence between the Dow's surge and the Nasdaq's decline highlighted uneven performance across different market segments, with traditional value stocks attracting renewed attention from investors seeking alternatives to high-valuation tech names.

Oil prices retreated during the session, providing relief to energy-sensitive sectors and supporting the broader market advance. The market rotation reflected shifting investor preferences as leadership broadened beyond the technology sector that had dominated gains in recent months.

The upcoming jobs report loomed as a key focal point for traders assessing the Federal Reserve's future policy decisions. Strong employment data could shift expectations for interest rates, while weakness might signal economic concerns about the labor market and broader economic growth. The report was expected to provide crucial insight into labor market conditions as the economy navigates current pressures.

The rotation away from technology stocks coincided with weakness in bitcoin, which fell to pre-Iran conflict lows as the cryptocurrency slid further. The digital asset was weathering what some described as its ugliest week in months as investment narratives shifted and liquidity rotated across markets.

Market participants were also monitoring developments in the cryptocurrency sector, where some strategists blamed artificial intelligence stocks for bitcoin's recent decline. The weakness in high-valuation tech names appeared to be extending beyond equities into digital assets as investors reassessed risk positioning.

The Dow's record close underscored the changing nature of market leadership. After months of technology stocks driving gains, traditional industrial and financial stocks took the spotlight, indicating a potential shift in investor preferences. This divergence between the performance of different market segments suggested investors were actively redeploying capital toward sectors that had lagged during the technology rally.

Looking ahead, the jobs report remained the key economic event on investors' radar as traders positioned for potential shifts in Federal Reserve policy and assessed the health of the labor market amid economic uncertainties.

cards.headline: Supreme Court Backs FCC Authority to Fine Telecom Companies
cards.teaser: The court ruled federal regulators can levy fines against cellphone carriers without providing quick jury trials.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 in favor of the Federal Communications Commission, upholding the agency's power to impose fines on wireless carriers. The decision rejected challenges from AT&T and Verizon, which argued that the FCC's in-house penalty proceedings violated their constitutional right to a jury trial.

The ruling preserves the FCC's existing administrative enforcement system, allowing the agency to continue levying penalties against telecommunications companies without requiring jury trials. The decision represented a victory for the Trump administration in the dispute over federal regulatory authority.

hero.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Israelis Escalate Protests Against Military Draft
hero.teaser: Rioting by Haredim over mandatory service has shocked many Israelis as the community intensifies resistance ahead of national elections.
hero.body:
Ultra-Orthodox Israelis have intensified their demonstrations against military conscription requirements, with a deadly incident during a recent Jerusalem protest highlighting the escalating tensions surrounding the issue.

Thousands of ultra-Orthodox Jews gathered in Jerusalem on Tuesday to protest a law requiring them to serve in the military. The demonstration turned tragic when a bus struck a crowd, killing a 14-year-old boy who became trapped underneath the vehicle. Police detained the bus driver and launched an investigation into the incident.

Video footage showed the bus driving directly into the assembled crowd of ultra-Orthodox men. According to police, the driver claimed he was assaulted by rioters before the incident occurred. Officers said a small group of protesters had begun violently disrupting public order by blocking traffic routes, damaging buses, setting fires to trash bins, and throwing objects at police and journalists at the scene.

The protests underscore deepening divisions within Israeli society as the country faces ongoing military manpower shortages following two years of conflict on multiple fronts. Ultra-Orthodox party leaders have consistently opposed conscription of religious students who pursue full-time Jewish text studies. Under a system established at Israel's founding in 1948, these students have traditionally received exemptions from mandatory military service.

This longstanding arrangement has become increasingly controversial among other Israelis, particularly as tens of thousands of conscripts and reservists have been mobilized across several military fronts despite a fragile ceasefire that ended the Gaza conflict.

The ultra-Orthodox population comprises 14 percent of Israel's Jewish population, and keeping their political parties in the government coalition remains crucial for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing coalition survival. Netanyahu faces pressure from opposition members and some coalition partners to expand military recruitment, but he relies on ultra-Orthodox parties for his parliamentary majority.

A new draft law was proposed in parliament's foreign affairs and defense committee after a previous conscription bill failed to pass in July. The United Torah Judaism party, a major ultra-Orthodox faction, withdrew from the government over that failed bill, reducing Netanyahu's coalition to 60 seats in the 120-seat parliament. Ministers from Shas, the other significant ultra-Orthodox party, resigned from cabinet positions over the conscription issue, though the party has not formally left the coalition.

Mass demonstrations against the conscription law have become regular occurrences in recent months as the debate intensifies. These protests highlight the competing priorities within Israeli society between military necessity and religious community autonomy, a tension that has grown more acute as security pressures mount and the need for soldiers increases.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Cease-Fire Between Israel and Lebanon
cards.teaser: Hezbollah rejected a cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon that was brokered by the United States, with the group's leader calling the truce a surrend.
cards.body:
Hezbollah rejected a cease-fire agreement between Israel and Lebanon announced by the United States following fresh diplomatic talks. The Iran-backed group's leader called the truce a surrender, noting that Hezbollah was excluded from the U.S.-brokered negotiations between the Israeli and Lebanese governments.

The rejection raises questions about the agreement's enforceability. A UN peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon, underscoring the ongoing security challenges in the region.

cards.headline: New Zealand Lawmakers Banned From China After Taiwan Visit
cards.teaser: China imposed a one-year travel ban on four legislators following their trip to Taiwan, surprising New Zealand's foreign minister.
cards.body:
China has imposed a one-year travel ban on four New Zealand lawmakers following their visit to Taiwan last month. New Zealand's foreign minister expressed surprise at the restriction, noting that lawmakers have visited Taiwan in previous years without facing such consequences.

The ban reflects China's increasingly assertive stance toward foreign officials who visit Taiwan, which Beijing considers part of its territory. New Zealand has traditionally maintained a delicate balance between its diplomatic and trade ties with China and its unofficial engagement with Taiwan, a position that has become increasingly challenging as regional tensions rise.

cards.headline: Boeing 787 Nose Gear Collapses at Frankfurt Airport
cards.teaser: A Lufthansa Dreamliner's nose gear failed at Frankfurt Airport, injuring several workers as the aircraft weighs up to 279 tons.
cards.body:
The nose gear on a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner operated by Lufthansa collapsed at Frankfurt Airport, injuring several workers. The airline said the cause of the accident is under investigation.

The 787-9 can weigh up to 279 tons at takeoff, making the collapse of landing gear a serious structural failure. The incident adds to ongoing scrutiny of Boeing's manufacturing and safety procedures across its aircraft fleet.

cards.headline: Colombia's Yellow Jersey Becomes Political Symbol in Presidential Race
cards.teaser: A presidential candidate endorsed by President Trump has been accused of co-opting the national soccer team's iconic yellow jersey.
cards.body:
Colombia's iconic yellow World Cup jersey, traditionally a source of national pride, is now at the center of a contentious presidential race. As the country prepares for the upcoming World Cup, the beloved soccer uniform has transformed into a political battleground.

A presidential candidate who received an endorsement from President Trump has faced criticism for using the yellow jersey in campaign materials. What was once a unifying cultural symbol has become divisive, with some Colombians viewing its political appropriation as turning a shared national treasure into a partisan tool.

cards.headline: Dubai Ruler's Nephew's Ex-Wife Goes Missing
cards.teaser: British lawyer David Haigh lost contact with Zeynab Javadli, and her Dubai home is now locked and empty.
cards.body:
British lawyer David Haigh lost contact with his client Zeynab Javadli on Tuesday. Her home in Dubai was found locked and empty, according to the BBC.

Haigh has been representing Javadli in legal proceedings connected to her divorce from a member of Dubai's ruling family.

cards.headline: French Open Sees All Top Seeds Eliminated
cards.teaser: The tournament has become unpredictable after all the big names were knocked out in early rounds.
cards.body:
The French Open lost all its top-seeded players in the early rounds, creating an unusually open field for the remainder of the tournament. The absence of the sport's biggest names has made the competition difficult to predict.

The unexpected eliminations have generated excitement among tennis fans as lesser-known players advance deeper into the draw. The tournament's outcome is now seen as wide open, with no clear favorite remaining in either the men's or women's competitions.

cards.headline: Murder trial begins for fatal stabbing at Texas high school track meet
cards.teaser: Prosecutors told jurors that Karmelo Anthony committed murder in the fatal stabbing of Austin Metcalf at a Frisco school track meet.
cards.body:
The murder trial of Karmelo Anthony opened in Texas with prosecutors arguing that the fatal stabbing of a teenager at a Frisco ISD track meet was murder, not self-defense. Austin Metcalf was killed during the incident at the school athletic event. Prosecutors described the attack as a sneak attack in their opening statements.

The jury selection process concluded without any Black jurors being seated, according to court observers. Opening statements have been completed and witness testimony has begun in the case. The defense is expected to argue self-defense, which prosecutors have already moved to counter in their presentation to the jury.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center directs staff to remove references to Trump from documents and signage
cards.teaser: An internal memo instructed Kennedy Center employees to immediately remove the president's name from the arts center by a set deadline.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center issued a memo directing staff to remove references to President Trump from signage, documents, and other materials at the performing arts center in Washington. Lawyers for the institution told employees that Trump's name must be removed from the facility by June 12, according to reports.

The directive comes as Trump's name has been disappearing from other public institutions and venues. The Kennedy Center, formally known as the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, is a national cultural institution that receives federal funding. The memo represents an immediate operational change for staff at the venue.

cards.headline: United jet was too slow and too low before Newark landing accident, investigators say
cards.teaser: Federal safety investigators found that a United Airlines 767 was flying below proper speed and altitude before striking a light pole while landing at Newark airport.
cards.body:
The National Transportation Safety Board determined that a United Airlines Boeing 767 captain was flying too slowly and at too low an altitude during approach to Newark Liberty International Airport last month. The aircraft struck a light pole during landing, which damaged a truck on the nearby New Jersey Turnpike.

The jet had flown from Italy before the incident occurred. The NTSB's findings identified speed and altitude management issues during the final approach phase as contributing factors to the accident.

cards.headline: Trump says Pulte will not serve permanently as national intelligence director
cards.teaser: President Trump clarified that Bill Pulte will not hold the position of director of national intelligence on a permanent basis.
cards.body:
President Trump stated that Bill Pulte will not be the permanent director of national intelligence, addressing concerns about the appointment that have sparked resistance among some Senate Republicans. Pulte's selection has led to what some describe as a rebellion within the GOP caucus.

Sources familiar with the situation have characterized Pulte as a partisan figure who has direct access to the president. The appointment has created tension on Capitol Hill, where senators from Trump's own party have expressed reservations about the choice for the sensitive intelligence position. Trump's statement appears aimed at easing concerns about the long-term leadership of the intelligence community.

cards.headline: Public health authorities weakened in some jurisdictions after pandemic restrictions
cards.teaser: Some state and local governments have reduced public health powers in response to criticism of lockdowns, mask mandates, and vaccine requirements during the pandemic.
cards.body:
Multiple U.S. jurisdictions have limited the authority of public health officials following criticism of pandemic-era measures. The restrictions targeted include lockdowns, school closures, mask mandates, and vaccine requirements that were used to control disease spread.

Public health experts worry these reduced powers could hamper responses to future disease outbreaks. The changes reflect an ongoing tension between emergency public health responses and concerns about individual liberties and economic impact.

cards.headline: Quantinuum Stock Closes Flat After Upsized Quantum Computing IPO
cards.teaser: The Honeywell-backed quantum computing company raised $1.68 billion but saw disappointing first-day trading results.
cards.body:
Quantinuum closed flat in its Nasdaq debut after completing an upsized initial public offering that raised $1.68 billion. The quantum computing company's stock offering was oversubscribed 20 times, reflecting strong investor demand before trading began.

The lackluster first-day performance surprised analysts who had anticipated a strong market reception given the enthusiasm during the IPO process. The company represents one of the first major quantum computing firms to enter public markets, backed by industrial conglomerate Honeywell.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls to Pre-Iran Conflict Low as Crypto Decline Extends
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency endured its worst week in months as investors rotated capital into other assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped to levels last seen before the Iran conflict began, extending a multiday decline that represents its ugliest week in months. The cryptocurrency fell as narratives supporting higher prices faded and liquidity shifted to other market segments.

Strategy's Michael Saylor attributed Bitcoin's decline to competition from AI stocks drawing investor attention. The price slump prompted crypto bears to celebrate, though some analysts cautioned against counting out the digital currency. Bitcoin's sagging price reflected broader rotation away from speculative assets.

cards.headline: Jamie Dimon to Pitch Investors on SpaceX IPO, Largest Ever Planned
cards.teaser: Wall Street banks are preparing to reap huge fees from Elon Musk's rocket company as it prepares its public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX is targeting the largest initial public offering in history, aiming to raise $75 billion from its stock market debut planned for June 12. The offering would value the rocket company at $1.77 trillion, marking a major milestone for Elon Musk's aerospace venture.

The blockbuster listing positions Musk, already the world's wealthiest person, to potentially become the first trillionaire. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon's personal involvement in pitching the deal underscores Wall Street's focus on the exceptional scale and significance of SpaceX's market entry.

cards.headline: Lululemon Cuts Annual Outlook, Cites Headwinds
cards.teaser: The athletic apparel company trimmed its forecast and issued weak second-quarter guidance ahead of its CEO transition.
cards.body:
Lululemon reduced its annual outlook and provided rough guidance for the second quarter, citing undisclosed headwinds facing the business. The downgrade added pressure to the athletic apparel retailer as it prepares for a leadership transition with a new CEO.

The company acknowledged that significant work remains needed for a turnaround, sending its stock lower. Lululemon's forecast cut reflected challenges in the retail environment and raised questions about the brand's growth trajectory after years of strong performance.

cards.headline: Netflix Shifts Movie Strategy to Fewer, Higher-Quality Films
cards.teaser: Film chief Dan Lin is greenlighting more movies than anyone while focusing on quality over quantity.
cards.body:
Netflix is implementing a new film strategy under Dan Lin, who leads the streaming service's movie division. Lin's approach emphasizes producing fewer films with higher quality standards, moving away from the platform's previous volume-focused model.

Despite the quality-over-quantity philosophy, Lin still greenlights more movies than any other studio executive. His strategy avoids writing blank checks for star-driven projects, instead focusing on films with strong creative foundations and commercial potential.

hero.headline: Fusion startup Helion raises $465 million to build power plant for Microsoft
hero.body:
Helion, a fusion energy startup supported by Sam Altman, has secured $465 million in funding to advance construction of a power plant intended to deliver electricity to Microsoft. The investment provides the company with crucial resources as it works toward completing the facility by 2028.

Fusion energy technology attempts to generate power by forcing atomic nuclei together, mirroring the energy production process of the sun. This approach differs fundamentally from nuclear fission, which splits atoms and generates radioactive waste. Fusion technology promises cleaner energy with reduced environmental impact, though the field has struggled for decades to achieve sustained commercial-scale energy production.

Helion has entered into an agreement with Microsoft to supply power from its planned fusion plant. The 2028 completion target is ambitious for an industry where similar projects typically require years or decades to reach operational status. The company must successfully demonstrate that its fusion technology operates reliably, generates electricity at scale, and can deliver power to Microsoft's facilities.

The funding round reflects increasing investor appetite for alternative energy solutions as organizations seek carbon-free power sources. Technology companies face mounting pressure to lower their environmental footprint while managing rising electricity consumption from data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure. Microsoft has announced aggressive climate commitments and is investigating multiple clean energy pathways, including nuclear and renewable options.

Helion operates within a growing field of fusion startups attempting to bring the technology to market. Other companies pursuing fusion development have secured backing from major investors and government support, though none has yet successfully operated a fusion facility that produces more energy than it consumes on a sustained basis. The $465 million funding round positions Helion to advance its technological approach, despite the company still facing substantial technical and regulatory obstacles before achieving power delivery to Microsoft by 2028.

The broader energy sector is experiencing renewed interest in fusion technology as demand for clean electricity accelerates. Large technology and AI companies including Google's parent Alphabet and OpenAI have invested in fusion ventures. This wave of investment comes as the artificial intelligence industry strains existing power grids, creating urgency around developing new energy sources.

The Trump administration has also signaled support for fusion development. Since taking office in January, the government has pursued deregulation of the nuclear energy industry and promoted technology advancement, including executive orders designating fusion development as a national security priority. The Department of Energy has established a new Office of Fusion aimed at preparing the technology for commercial deployment as rapidly as possible.

Despite investor enthusiasm and government backing, fusion energy remains commercially unproven. No utility-scale fusion plant currently operates, and some scientists remain skeptical about achieving commercial viability. Helion's aggressive timeline and substantial funding position it as a significant contender in the race to commercialize fusion energy technology.

cards.headline: Apple approves first AI agent for Messages for Business platform
cards.teaser: Poke becomes the first AI agent authorized to operate on Apple's Messages for Business, allowing users to interact with AI through text messages.
cards.body:
Apple has approved Poke as the first AI agent to operate on its Messages for Business platform. The startup enables users to access AI agent services through text messages, integrating automated assistance directly into Apple's messaging infrastructure.

This approval represents a significant step in expanding AI capabilities within Apple's ecosystem. iPhone owners can now leverage AI agent functionality through the Messages app, bringing intelligent automation to one of the most widely used communication channels on the platform.

cards.headline: Meta builds data centers in tents to reduce costs
cards.teaser: Meta has adopted an unconventional approach to data center construction by using tents, a strategy previously employed by Tesla.
cards.body:
Meta is constructing data centers using tents as a cost-cutting measure. The approach mirrors a tactic used by Tesla and represents an attempt to reduce the massive expenses associated with traditional data center infrastructure.

The tent-based construction method could significantly lower Meta's capital expenditures for data center facilities. The company operates extensive computing infrastructure to support its social media platforms and artificial intelligence systems, making data center costs a major line item in its budget.

cards.headline: Bumblebees demonstrate problem-solving abilities in new study
cards.teaser: Scientists in Finland found that bumblebees can spontaneously solve problems, completing an insect version of a classic cognitive test.
cards.body:
Researchers in Finland discovered that bumblebees can spontaneously solve complex problems despite their tiny brains. The scientists tested the insects using an adapted version of the box-and-banana problem, a classic experiment typically used to assess problem-solving in primates and other animals.

The findings suggest bumblebees possess cognitive abilities comparable to some primates in specific problem-solving contexts. The research adds to growing evidence that insects can perform sophisticated mental tasks previously thought to require larger brains, challenging assumptions about the relationship between brain size and cognitive capability.

cards.headline: Sun releases three major solar flares, raising aurora chances across US
cards.teaser: The sun erupted with three large solar flares in under 24 hours, increasing the likelihood of northern lights visible in 23 states.
cards.body:
The sun produced three significant solar flares in less than 24 hours, sending charged particles toward Earth. The activity originates from what scientists describe as an unusual anti-Hale sunspot, creating what researchers call a cannibal coronal mass ejection that is expected to reach Earth.

The solar activity increases the probability of auroras appearing across much of the United States. Space weather forecasters indicate that northern lights could be visible in 23 states as the charged particles interact with Earth's magnetic field. The flares prompted space weather conditions to return to elevated levels with additional M-class flares recorded.

cards.headline: Elon Musk seeks to end FTC oversight of X data practices
cards.teaser: Musk is making another attempt to terminate Federal Trade Commission audits of how X handles user data, drawing warnings from public commenters.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has filed a new petition seeking to end FTC audits of X's data handling practices. Public commenters responding to the filing warned the agency that Musk cannot be trusted to protect user privacy on the platform formerly known as Twitter.

The FTC conducts periodic audits of X as part of oversight stemming from previous privacy violations. Musk's latest effort to escape this supervision represents a renewed push to remove federal scrutiny of the company's data security measures and user privacy protections.

cards.headline: Google launches customizable search profiles for creators and publishers
cards.teaser: Google is allowing social media stars, creators, and publishers to customize how their content appears in search results through new profile pages.
cards.body:
Google has introduced customizable search profiles that allow creators and publishers to control how they appear in search results. The feature lets content producers highlight their work and personalize their search presence.

The launch addresses concerns from creators about visibility as Google integrates more AI features into search. AI-generated summaries in search results have reduced traffic to original content sources, making an official Google Search presence increasingly valuable for maintaining audience reach.

hero.headline: Liverpool appoint Andoni Iraola as head coach after sacking Arne Slot
hero.body:
Liverpool have confirmed the appointment of Andoni Iraola as their new head coach on a two-year contract. The 43-year-old Spaniard takes over just six days after the club parted ways with Arne Slot, moving quickly to secure their preferred candidate.

Liverpool identified Iraola as the ideal fit for their desired playing style and moved decisively to appoint him ahead of competition from other top clubs. Milan, Bayer Leverkusen and Crystal Palace had all expressed interest in the former Bournemouth manager. While other coaches including Stuttgart's Sebastian Hoeness and Pierre Sage of Lens were considered, Iraola was Liverpool's favored option from the outset and the only candidate formally spoken to about the position.

Sporting director Richard Hughes led Liverpool's approach for Iraola, having previously worked with him at Bournemouth in 2023. Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football for Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group, conducted a review following the team's poor title defense under Slot. They concluded that a change was necessary to implement a more aggressive, attacking style of play.

Negotiations progressed smoothly after formal talks began earlier in the week. Iraola made clear from the beginning that Liverpool were his only target after his contract with Bournemouth expired. The straightforward process was aided by Hughes's close working relationship with Iraola's agent Iñaki Ibáñez, who also represents Xabi Alonso.

Speaking about his appointment, Iraola stated: "At the beginning when you arrive at any club, I think you need to kind of prove a little bit yourself. You need to earn the right also to belong. I want to do this as quickly as possible so I can also celebrate with them."

He added on his ambitions: "I think Liverpool gives me the chance to coach top players, and top players give you the chance to fight for titles. To win titles. Obviously when you arrive at a place, you cannot promise everything. But it's true that I understand where I'm coming and what is expected. I'm ready for the challenge."

Iraola has signed a contract that runs until the end of the 2027/28 season. The two-year length reflects his preferred approach to managing his career, following the pattern he established at both Bournemouth and Rayo Vallecano.

The new manager intends to bring his backroom team from Bournemouth to Anfield, including assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper, analyst Tom Webber and fitness coach Pablo de la Torre. Liverpool have not yet finalized all additions to their coaching staff.

Liverpool believe Iraola is one of the best coaches available and well-suited to evolving their team's style. His track record at Bournemouth of developing players and building an exciting, high-pressing team without significant financial resources particularly appealed to the club's leadership.

cards.headline: Ollie Robinson takes four wickets on England return as New Zealand struggles at Lord's
cards.teaser: Ollie Robinson marked his return to Test cricket with four wickets as New Zealand closed day one at 61-6, trailing England by 79 runs.
cards.body:
Ollie Robinson marked his return to England Test cricket with an outstanding performance at Lord's, claiming four wickets on the opening day of the first Test against New Zealand. The fast bowler took three wickets in his opening over, a triple-wicket maiden that proved decisive as New Zealand collapsed to 61-6 by close of play.

Robinson's recall came after more than two years away from international cricket. The bowler has spoken about rediscovering his love of the game during his time away, and his impressive comeback gave England a commanding position in the match, with New Zealand trailing by 79 runs.

cards.headline: Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open final as first qualifier to advance at Roland Garros
cards.teaser: Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska defeated Diana Shnaider to become the first qualifier to reach the French Open final, extending her remarkable tournament run.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Maja Chwalinska made history at the French Open by becoming the first qualifier ever to reach the final at Roland Garros. The Polish player defeated 25th seed Diana Shnaider 7-6 (4), 6-4 in the semifinals, advancing to Saturday's championship match against Mirra Andreeva.

The emotional victory saw Chwalinska sobbing into her towel after the match—a raw display of the magnitude of her achievement. Her improbable run through the tournament has captured attention as she stands one win away from an unthinkable Grand Slam title.

cards.headline: Northern Ireland defeats Guinea 1-0 despite Tom Atcheson red card
cards.teaser: Northern Ireland secured a 1-0 victory over Guinea in an international friendly despite playing with ten men after Tom Atcheson's dismissal.
cards.body:
Northern Ireland earned a 1-0 win over Guinea in an international friendly, showing resilience after going down to ten men. Manager Michael O'Neill praised his team's character following the victory, though he acknowledged that Tom Atcheson's red card significantly altered the match. O'Neill stated the dismissal killed the game as a contest.

The friendly provided Northern Ireland with valuable preparation despite the numerical disadvantage for a significant portion of the match. The team managed to hold onto their lead and secure the clean sheet victory even while playing a man down against the African opposition.

cards.headline: Caleb Williams named Madden NFL 27 cover athlete
cards.teaser: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was revealed as the cover athlete for Madden NFL 27, fulfilling what he described as a childhood dream.
cards.body:
Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears was announced as the cover athlete for Madden NFL 27. The quarterback described the honor as living out a childhood dream after being selected for one of gaming's most iconic covers. Williams channeled Michael Jordan in the cover imagery, connecting his role with Chicago sports history.

EA Sports used the announcement to also tease the introduction of the tush push play in the upcoming game. The cover reveal marks a significant milestone in Williams' career as he joins the roster of players who have been featured on the popular football video game franchise.

cards.headline: UFC 329 adds lightweight bout to McGregor vs. Holloway card
cards.teaser: UFC 329 featuring the main event between Conor McGregor and Max Holloway added a lightweight matchup between a veteran and knockout artist.
cards.body:
A new lightweight bout was added to the UFC 329 card headlined by Conor McGregor versus Max Holloway. The matchup pairs a veteran lightweight fighter against a knockout artist, adding depth to the event's fight lineup.

The addition strengthens the overall card as UFC continues to build out the event featuring the high-profile main event between former champion McGregor and Holloway. The organization continues to add fights to the card as the event date approaches.

cards.headline: Liverpool make contact with RB Leipzig over Yan Diomande transfer
cards.teaser: Liverpool reached out to RB Leipzig regarding a potential move for midfielder Yan Diomande as transfer activity picks up.
cards.body:
Liverpool have intensified their interest in defender Yan Diomande by making contact with RB Leipzig regarding a potential transfer. The move represents a significant step in the club's pursuit of the player.

This development comes as Liverpool continue to strengthen their defensive options in the ongoing transfer window.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Author of Persepolis, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and graphic novelist whose memoir Persepolis transformed international understanding of Iran, has died at age 56. Her family stated that she "died of sadness" following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away on April 8 of the previous year. In the weeks after his death, Satrapi posted on Instagram: "For I lost the love of my life."

Born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, near the Caspian Sea, Satrapi grew up in Tehran with her father, an engineer, and her mother, a dress designer. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and shield her from the restrictions of the Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France, arriving in 1994 and becoming a French citizen in 2006.

Satrapi published Persepolis in 2000 as a comic book memoir that became an international publishing sensation. The work chronicled her rebellious childhood during Iran's revolution and its aftermath, following her experience of the country's violence and ideological control before she was sent alone to Europe at age 14. The memoir sold millions of copies and established Satrapi as one of the world's most widely read Iranian authors.

When asked about her intentions for the work, Satrapi told the Guardian in 2024 that she wanted Western readers to recognize Iranian people as human beings like themselves. In a 2020 interview with El País, she recalled having minimal expectations for publication, saying: "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher. I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read."

The animated film adaptation, which Satrapi co-directed, became an international success and made her the first woman nominated for an Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. She explained that her purpose in creating comics was to reassure young Iranians they were heard and supported globally, asking: "If they kill you and the whole world doesn't care, how is that?"

Beyond comics, Satrapi directed five feature films, including Radioactive (2019), which starred Rosamund Pike as scientist Marie Curie. After stepping away from comics for years, she returned to the medium in 2024, coordinating Woman, Life, Freedom, a collaborative graphic work created by 17 Iranian and international comic artists alongside academics. The book examined the protest movement following the 2022 death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a Kurdish-Iranian woman. Satrapi stated: "The only thing I can do is cultural work. This book is a message to the Iranian people to say, listen, you are not alone."

Tributes came from across French politics and culture. President Emmanuel Macron described her as "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale." Margaret Atwood told the Guardian that Persepolis made an enormous impact, noting that while she only wrote about oppression in theocratic regimes, Satrapi lived it.

cards.headline: 60 Minutes Boss Promises Independence After Correspondent Firings
cards.teaser: The new executive producer of 60 Minutes pledged to uphold editorial independence as CBS waits to see if remaining correspondents will stay.
cards.body:
The new executive producer of 60 Minutes sent a memo vowing to pursue stories without fear or favor and to resist instruction from company ownership on sensitive reports. The statement came amid significant turmoil at the CBS News program following the recent firings of three correspondents.

Fired correspondent Scott Pelley accused CBS executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting. With four of the show's seven full-time correspondents now gone—Pelley, Sharyn Alfonsi, and Cecilia Vega fired, and Anderson Cooper having departed earlier—CBS News staffers are questioning whether the remaining correspondents will stay and how the program will continue its 59th season beginning in September.

cards.headline: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Overwhelms Ticketing Systems
cards.teaser: Advance ticket sales for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey created technical problems at AMC, with wait times initially reaching an hour.
cards.body:
Demand for advance tickets to Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey caused significant technical disruptions across AMC's digital platforms. Wait times initially stretched to an hour before dropping to eight minutes as the system stabilized. Buyers encountered multiple error messages while attempting to purchase seats for the highly anticipated film.

The Odyssey will play a three-week engagement at Westwood Village Theatre in 70mm format, with the Seattle International Film Festival also bringing back 70mm screenings for the release.

cards.headline: Starz Orders Power: Legacy Series
cards.teaser: Starz greenlit Power: Legacy, reuniting actors Joseph Sikora and Michael Rainey Jr. for an eight-episode first season.
cards.body:
Starz approved production of Power: Legacy, a new series in the Power franchise. The show will follow the reunion of Tommy Egan, played by Joseph Sikora, and Tariq St. Patrick, played by Michael Rainey Jr. Tariq is the son of Tommy's late friend James Ghost St. Patrick from the original series.

The network ordered eight episodes for the first season. Both actors previously led their own spinoff series within the Power universe. The new show marks another expansion of the franchise, which has generated multiple successful spinoffs for the network.

cards.headline: Universal Music Buys Back $290.5 Million in Stock From Bill Ackman
cards.teaser: Universal Music will repurchase over 14.2 million shares from Pershing Square after rejecting the fund's takeover proposal.
cards.body:
Universal Music announced it will repurchase approximately $290.5 million worth of stock from Pershing Square, the capital fund founded by billionaire investor Bill Ackman. The buyback involves over 14.2 million shares valued at roughly 250 million euros.

The transaction follows Universal Music's rejection of a takeover proposal from Pershing Square. The world's largest record company is moving to reduce Ackman's stake in the company following the failed acquisition attempt. The stock repurchase represents a significant restructuring of ownership at the music giant.

cards.headline: Anna Faris and Son Jack Pratt Make Rare Red Carpet Appearance
cards.teaser: Anna Faris appeared with her 13-year-old son Jack Pratt at the Scary Movie 6 premiere, marking his first public appearance in nine years.
cards.body:
Anna Faris brought her son Jack Pratt to the premiere of Scary Movie 6, where the 13-year-old nearly matched his mother's height. Jack is the son of Faris and actor Chris Pratt. The appearance marked his first red carpet moment in nine years.

Faris wore a side-baring black dress for the premiere. The rare public appearance with her son drew attention from multiple entertainment outlets covering the event. Jack had largely stayed out of the public eye since his last red carpet appearance as a young child.

cards.headline: Dateline to Investigate Luigi Mangione Case
cards.teaser: A Dateline special airing Friday will examine the investigation into Luigi Mangione, exploring how public reaction has varied

hero.headline: House Oversight releases transcript of Bondi interview on Epstein files
hero.teaser: The transcript shows the former attorney general declined to answer multiple questions during the four-hour closed-door session.
hero.body:
The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee released a transcript Thursday from its closed-door meeting with former Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the handling of Jeffrey Epstein files. The transcript provides the first public account of Bondi's testimony on the matter.

During the roughly four-hour session, Bondi declined to answer numerous questions. She directed responsibility to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche regarding how the files were handled.

The release of the transcript came after a contentious period between Bondi and the committee. The House panel had initially scheduled Bondi for a deposition on April 14, but the Justice Department informed the committee that she would not appear. The department argued that because Bondi no longer held the position of attorney general, the subpoena no longer applied since it had been issued in her official capacity.

The committee's Democrats responded by filing a civil contempt resolution against Bondi for not appearing at the scheduled deposition. Representative Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the committee, announced the action and stated that Bondi had "illegally defied our committee, skipped her deposition, and has refused to cooperate."

However, shortly after the Democrats announced the contempt charges, the oversight committee revealed that Bondi would appear before the panel on May 29. Republicans on the committee said the contempt action was "completely unnecessary" given that Bondi was now scheduled to testify. The oversight Democrats noted the timing, writing that the appearance was announced just 45 minutes after they filed the contempt charges.

Bondi had been subpoenaed by the committee while still serving as attorney general. The committee's chair, Republican Representative James Comer, wrote in the subpoena letter that there were questions regarding the Justice Department's handling of the Epstein investigation and its compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The Justice Department faced criticism over its compliance with that law after failing to meet a December 19 deadline to release relevant files. The department instead released what it said were the full files on January 31. Survivors of Epstein's abuse raised concerns that sensitive personal information was improperly disclosed in the files, while several lawmakers criticized some of the redactions included in the documents.

According to Democrat Garcia, Bondi had "extensive personal knowledge about the Trump administration's handling of the Epstein files," making her testimony and cooperation crucial regardless of her current job title.

The Justice Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the matter.

cards.headline: House Democrats join Republicans to defeat Lebanon war powers resolution
cards.teaser: The House of Representatives defeated a resolution Thursday that would have constrained the Trump administration's military authority in Lebanon.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives defeated a resolution Thursday that would have limited the Trump administration's military authority in Lebanon. Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the measure, but it failed after most House Democrats joined Republicans in voting against it.

The vote exposed divisions within the Democratic caucus over Middle East policy. Democratic leadership opposed the resolution, contrasting with their support for a similar Iran war powers measure that passed the previous day. The outcome leaves the Trump administration with continued flexibility to conduct military operations in Lebanon without additional congressional constraints.

cards.headline: Trump says Bill Pulte will serve temporarily as intelligence chief
cards.teaser: The president addressed bipartisan controversy over his choice for director of national intelligence.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Thursday that Bill Pulte, his selection for director of national intelligence, would hold the position on a temporary basis. The announcement came as Trump fielded questions from reporters in the Oval Office.

The choice has drawn criticism from lawmakers across the aisle. Trump defended Pulte's qualifications, characterizing him as intelligent and possessing strong integrity. Pulte currently leads the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

cards.headline: Senator Collins breaks with GOP on insurance oversight amendment
cards.teaser: The Maine Republican voted for a Democratic amendment to investigate insurance companies denying medical care.
cards.body:
Sen. Susan Collins of Maine broke ranks with Republican leadership Thursday, voting for a Democratic amendment to direct a $70 billion budget reconciliation package to the Judiciary Committee. The amendment aimed to investigate insurance companies' practices of denying medical care to patients.

Collins was the sole Republican to support the measure. As a senator facing reelection, her vote represented a notable split from her party's leadership on the issue.

cards.headline: Trump says he saw no cognitive decline in Biden during transition
cards.teaser: The president told reporters he did not detect issues when he met with Biden after the 2024 election.
cards.body:
President Trump told reporters Thursday that he observed no cognitive decline in former President Biden during their November 2024 transition meeting following Trump's election victory. Trump said Biden appeared consistent with how he had seemed for an extended period.

Trump made the remarks when asked whether he had detected any cognitive issues at their meeting. The comment comes as Biden's mental fitness remained a topic of public discussion during his final year in office.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary Thursday for governor of New Mexico. Haaland's victory sets up a general election campaign where she could make history.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously represented New Mexico in the House of Representatives before joining the Biden cabinet.

cards.headline: Poll finds 22 percent do not consider themselves proud Americans
cards.teaser: The Quinnipiac survey showed divided views on patriotism ahead of the country's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
A Quinnipiac University poll released Thursday found that 22 percent of Americans do not consider themselves proud Americans, while 73 percent said they do. The survey was conducted ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary this summer.

The poll revealed significant differences in patriotism levels across demographic groups, offering insight into American attitudes about national pride as the country approaches this milestone anniversary.
